Package org.efs.io

package org.efs.io

Event File System I/O Package

The org.efs.io package provides the core I/O capabilities for the Event File System (EFS). It defines a persistent event store that indexes events by both publish timestamp and row index, enabling efficient retrieval of events within specified time intervals and supporting both historical event retrieval and live event delivery.

Core Components

EfsFile
Central class for managing event storage and retrieval. EfsFile stores IEfsEvent instances indexed by publish timestamp and monotonically increasing row index. Each row is unique by row index, while publish timestamps may be duplicated but are guaranteed to increase monotonically. The class is thread-safe and uses CQEngine for efficient indexed queries.
EfsFileConnection
EfsFile access point for agents. Agents use this connection to add and retrieve events to and from the efs event file based on the access mode used to create the connection.
EfsRow
Encapsulates a stored event along with its metadata: publish timestamp and unique row index. EfsRow is the unit of storage returned during event retrieval operations.
EfsInterval
Defines a temporal or index-based interval for retrieving events. Supports flexible interval specification using fixed times, relative durations, or index offsets, with inclusive or exclusive endpoint boundaries.
EfsIntervalEndpoint
Represents a single endpoint of an EfsInterval. Endpoints can be specified as fixed timestamps, time-relative offsets, or row index offsets.

Event Retrieval Pattern

The package supports a flexible event retrieval model:

  • Historical Events: Retrieve events that have already been stored within a specified time interval or index range.
  • Live Events: Subscribe to future events matching specified criteria and are published after the retrieval request is initiated.
  • Hybrid Retrieval: Retrieve both historical events and subscribe to future events in a single request.

Retrieval is controlled through Retrieval subscriptions returned from EfsFile.retrieve.

Creating a Retrieval Query

EfsFile stores IEfsEvent-implementing objects in a cqengine IndexCollection. EfsFile.retrieve access a user Query which use Attribute to retrieve values from IndexCollection values. But there is a catch:

EfsFile stores event within an EfsRow and the row is stored in IndexCollection.

This means that creating Attribute instances directly from the stored event class will not work because the event class is not stored directly in the index collection. What is worse, providing a query based on such attributes results in asynchronous retrieval failures.

The solution is to use event attributes generated by efs file. These attributes can be accessed via EfsFile.attribute(String field) where field is the event field name. If the event has a getter method long getId(), then the field name is "id". Below sample code shows how to create a user query for UserLoginEvent.

EfsFile generates cqengine attributes for event fields based on the @CQAttribute annotation. This annotation has three fields:

  1. attribute: defines cqengine attribute type. This includes: simple, simple (nullable), multi-value, and multi-value (nullable).
  2. org.efs.io.CQAttribute#nullValues nullValues: set to true if attribute type is CQAttributeType.MULTIVALUE_NULLABLE where field returns an Iterable containing null values. Default setting is false. This field is ignored for all other attribute types.
  3. org.efs.io.CQAttribute#index index defines cqengine index type applied to the attribute. Default setting is no index.

See cqengine GitHub project page for further explanation on attributes and indices.

Usage Example

Here is a typical usage pattern for adding events and retrieving them: 

import org.efs.event.EfsTopicKey;
 import org.efs.dispatcher.IEfsAgent;
 import org.efs.event.IEfsEvent;
 import org.efs.io.EfsFile;
 import org.efs.io.EfsFile.AccessMode;
 import org.efs.io.EfsRow;
 import org.efs.io.EfsInterval;
 import org.efs.io.EfsTimeEndpoint;
 import org.efs.io.EfsIntervalEndpoint.EndpointType;
 import org.efs.io.EfsIntervalEndpoint.Clusivity;
 import com.googlecode.cqengine.query.Query;
 import static com.googlecode.cqengine.query.QueryFactory.startsWith;
 import java.time.Instant;
 import java.util.concurrent.atomic.AtomicInteger;

 // Define a custom event class implementing IEfsEvent
 public final class UserLoginEvent implements IEfsEvent {
     private final String userId;
     private final String ipAddress;
     private final long timestamp;

     public UserLoginEvent(String userId, String ipAddress, long timestamp) {
         this.userId = userId;
         this.ipAddress = ipAddress;
         this.timestamp = timestamp;
     }

     // Getter methods for fields "userId", "ipAddress", and "timestamp".
     // Define cqengine attribute type and index type used for efs-generated attributes and indicies.
     // If there is no
     @CqAttribute (attribute = CQAttributeType.SIMPLE, index = CQIndexType.HASH_INDEX)
     public String getUserId() { return userId; }

     @CqAttribute (attribute = CQAttributeType.SIMPLE, index = CQIndexType.RADIX_TREE_INDEX)
     public String getIpAddress() { return ipAddress; }

     @CqAttribute (attribute = CQAttributeType.SIMPLE, index = CQIndexType.NAVIGABLE_INDEX)
     public long getTimestamp() { return timestamp; }
 }

 // Define an application agent implementing IEfsAgent for processing retrieved UserLoginEvent rows.
 public final class AppAgent implements IEfsAgent {
     private final AtomicInteger eventCount = new AtomicInteger(0);

     public void onUserLogin(final EfsRow<UserLoginEvent> row) {
         UserLoginEvent event = row.getEvent();
         System.out.println("Event at index " + row.getRowIndex() +
                            " published at " + row.getPublishTimestamp() +
                            ": User " + event.getUserId() +
                            " logged in from " + event.getIpAddress());
         eventCount.incrementAndGet();
     }

     public void onDone(final RetrievalCompleteEvent<UserLoginEvent> event) {
         System.out.println("Retrieval complete. Total events: " + eventCount.get());
         System.out.println("Completion type: " + completionEvent.completionType());
     }
 }

 // In your application:

 // 1. Create or open an EfsFile for a specific topic and event type
 EfsTopicKey<UserLoginEvent> topicKey =
     new EfsTopicKey<>("user.login", UserLoginEvent.class);

 EfsFile<UserLoginEvent> eventFile =
     EfsFile.openEventFile(topicKey, "default-dispatcher");

 // 2. Open connection to file.
 EfsFileConnection<UserLoginEvent> connection =
     eventFile.connect(AccessMode.READ_WRITE, agent);

 // 3. Add events to the file
 AppAgent agent = new AppAgent();
 Instant now = eventFile.instant();

 eventFile.add(new UserLoginEvent("user123", "192.168.1.100", System.currentTimeMillis()));
 eventFile.add(new UserLoginEvent("user456", "10.0.0.50", System.currentTimeMillis()));

 // 4. Retrieve events using an interval and query condition
 // Define an interval: all events from 1 hour ago to now (inclusive)
 Instant oneHourAgo = now.minusSeconds(3600);
 EfsInterval interval = new EfsInterval(
     new EfsTimeEndpoint(oneHourAgo, Clusivity.INCLUSIVE),
     new EfsTimeEndpoint(now, Clusivity.INCLUSIVE)
 );
 Attribute<EfsRow<UserLoginEvent>, String> ipaddrAttribute = (Attribute<EfsRow<UserLoginEvent>, String>) eventFile.attribute("ipAddress");
 Query ipQuery = startsWith(ipaddrAttribute, "192.168.1");

 // 5. Process retrieved events with callbacks
 try (var retrieval = eventFile.retrieve(interval,
                                         ipQuery,            // User logging in from local IP address.
                                         agent::onUserLogin, // Event callback: invoked for each matching event
                                         agent::onDone);     // Completion callback: invoked when retrieval is finished
     // Retrieval is now active and subscribed
     // New events published during the retrieval interval will be delivered
 }

Key Features

Efficient Indexing
Events are indexed by both publish timestamp (hash index) and row index (unique index), enabling fast queries on both dimensions.
Flexible Intervals
Intervals can be specified using fixed timestamps, durations relative to the latest event, or row index offsets, providing flexibility for various retrieval scenarios.
Thread-Safe Operations
EfsFile is annotated with @ThreadSafe and uses atomic operations and concurrent data structures to ensure safe concurrent access.
Event Filtering
Beyond interval filtering, events can be filtered using CQEngine queries on event properties, allowing fine-grained control over which events are retrieved.
Live Subscription Support
Retrieval requests can remain active to receive new events as they are published, enabling real-time event delivery patterns.
Dispatcher Integration
All event operations are coordinated through an EfsDispatcher, ensuring thread-safe, ordered processing of events and retrieval requests.

Exception Handling

The package defines clear exception semantics:

  • NullPointerException is thrown when required arguments are null.
  • IllegalArgumentException is thrown for invalid arguments (e.g., invalid dispatcher names).
  • IllegalStateException is thrown when operations are performed in invalid states (e.g., agent not registered with dispatcher)
